turnaround_reason: Coty was beaten down on soft prestige-fragrance sell-through, mass-beauty share loss (CoverGirl/Rimmel), and a debt overhang from its legacy P&G-beauty acquisition. The recovering thesis: deleveraging is working and the portfolio is being rationalized, but growth remains anemic.
bullish_points: Q4 FY26 beat: like-for-like sales -1% vs guidance of mid-single-digit decline; strong cash generation
Meaningful deleveraging — net debt down ~$840M YoY to $2.9B, leverage ~3.4x with a stated ~2x long-term target; FY26 FCF $348M (+~$70M YoY)
Trades below book (P/B 0.82) and at ~10x forward earnings; JAB majority ownership aligns with a patient value fix
Returning Gucci Beauty license to Kering for ~$400M ($250M upfront) — cleans up a low-margin obligation and adds cash
bearish_points: Management declined to issue FY27 guidance amid 'Coty Curated' rollout and strategic review — reduced visibility is a red flag for a leveraged name
Prestige fragrance sell-out -1% in H2; flagship launches not yet creating portfolio halo
Gucci exit removes a low-double-digit % of revenue by FY28 with a sizable mechanical profit hit absent offsets
Current ratio 0.755 and total debt $3.3B keep the balance sheet fragile; operating margin still negative TTM
catalyst: Q1 FY27 earnings and any strategic-review outcome (further brand divestitures / capital-structure actions); evidence that deleveraging continues without volume collapse
catalyst_timing: Next earnings 2026-11-05; strategic review ongoing through FY27
suggested_trade: Small starter spot around $2.60-2.80 as a deleveraging/deep-value play; size for volatility given sub-$3 price and leverage. Spot only — no need to reach for options here.
key_risk: Fragrance/mass volumes deteriorate faster than debt comes down, so leverage re-rates the equity lower despite the cheap multiple (classic levered value trap).
would_skip_if: Leverage stops falling, another guidance withdrawal/cut lands, or LFL sales turn sharply negative — any of which breaks the deleveraging thesis.
